result.process_description:
Title: Farming Bot

Players want to create custom farming bots, that help them gather resources.
First you have to find out which resources you want.
Up to 10 resources in parallel can be collected, some resources are more urgently needed than others.
Some resources are required to create tools that are needed to gather other resources (create a custom logic of the dependencies in your game).
After all preferences are collected, your bot starts farming.
Sometimes,  random natural disasters strike and set your bot back.
Whenever some milestones are reached, you are notified.
During farming it is possible to update the list of to be farmed materials (at all times).
After the bot is finished, you should be able to brag to selected friends and/or send them materials.

result.rule: Each lane flowNodeRef identifies a node in the owning process. Assign nodes according to stated responsibility and avoid arbitrary membership.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.

result.rule: When the description ... one participant states choices and then sets up an automated component, and that same component later carries out its own activities inside the same flow, instead of only exchanging messages with the participant: Model one pool that contains the whole flow, with one lane for the human participant and one lane for the automated component. Place the participant's steps in the participant's lane and the component's own activities in the component's lane. Use a single start event in the lane of the participant who initiates the flow, and connect steps across lanes with sequence flows. Do not add a separate start event for the component's setup and do not place the component in its own pool.

When the description states that the process is started by a participant performing an action of their own, such as submitting or entering information, and that the system then acts on that input: Keep the start event as the process trigger, and model the participant's performed action as a task (user task if it is a manual entry) placed after the start event and before the system tasks that process the input. Do not name the start event after that action or use the start event to stand for the action.

When the description states that the process begins with a participant performing an action that the description itself presents as work carried out by that participant: Model the start as an unlabeled start event followed by a task that performs the described action (a user task when the participant works through a system). Do not put the action into the start event label, since that would drop the performed work from the flow.

When the description says the process begins when a participant's need or condition arises (a state the participant notices or is in), and the performed actions that follow are described separately: Model the start event with a label that names the arising condition as a state, in the description's wording, rather than the participant's later action or a generic 'participant performs X' phrase. Keep the participant's performed actions as tasks placed after the start event, and do not use the start event label to stand for those actions.
